text: The Hebrew Bible tells of one God who made a covenant, a binding agreement, with the people of Israel.
In its story, Moses led the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt and received the Torah from God.
src: whose Hebrew Bible tells of one God who made a covenant with them / a covenant, a binding agreement
the Israelites, enslaved in Egypt, were freed under the leadership of Moses, received the Torah from God at Mount Sinai

text: By the Bible’s account, King Solomon built the First Temple in Jerusalem more than 2,900 years ago.
Later the Babylonians destroyed it and took many people far away into exile.
src: c. 10th century BCE: By the biblical account, David makes Jerusalem his capital and Solomon builds the First Temple
586 BCE: The Babylonians destroy Jerusalem and the First Temple and take many Judeans into exile

text: After the Romans destroyed the Second Temple, rabbis, teachers of the law, rebuilt Jewish life around prayer and study.
In the synagogue, the Torah is read from a handwritten scroll all through the year.
src: After the destruction of the Second Temple by Rome in 70 CE, the rabbis rebuilt Judaism around the synagogue, prayer and the study of the Torah and the Talmud / The rabbi, a teacher of the law rather than a priest
The Torah, in the narrow sense of the five books, is read in the synagogue from a handwritten scroll in a cycle that runs through the year

text: Morning and evening, Jews say the Shema: “Hear, O Israel: the Lord is our God, the Lord is one.”
They keep the Sabbath, a day of rest from Friday evening to Saturday evening.
src: The Shema, recited morning and evening, declares: “Hear, O Israel: the Lord is our God, the Lord is one.”
the observance of the Sabbath, the day of rest from Friday evening to Saturday evening

text: Jews came to live in many lands, where they were sometimes treated cruelly and even driven out, as from Spain.
In the Holocaust, Nazi Germany and its helpers murdered about six million Jews.
src: In the Middle Ages Jewish communities spread across the Islamic world and Christian Europe / In Christian Europe Jews faced periods of tolerance and of savage persecution / expulsions, from England in 1290, France in the 14th century and Spain in 1492

text: Today about 15 million Jews live in the world, most of them in Israel and the United States.
Hebrew, the language of their prayers, is spoken again as the language of Israel.
